terra.problem: Saying the trouble is in the room and not in a palace adds locations Peter does not give.
The claim that Israel had plenty of wicked kings needs a reference outside this passage.
Secretly does not mean nobody sees it coming. Peter also does not give that as his reason for warning them.
The explanation attributes the defamation specifically to the many followers, while the text leaves that connection open.
Peter calls the words deceptive, but does not say they sound good.
The claim that Egypt had plenty of kings needs a reference outside this passage.
Peter says Lot saw and heard lawless deeds, not that he saw it all.
The cities and the ancient world are described as destroyed, not as being held. Peter specifically says the angels were held for judgment.
The claim that they have no second thoughts adds a state of mind Peter does not give.
Saying the false teachers show no restraint at all goes beyond Peter's statement that they are unafraid to slander glorious beings.
Years of study would not necessarily mean they understood the matters.
Peter does not say whether the false teachers learned anything from angels. The explanation asserts that they did not.
Carousing in broad daylight does not establish that they do no hiding or that they feel comfortable doing it.
Saying they do not bother to hide it adds an attitude Peter does not state.
The cookie-box joke puts a made-up object into the Bible scene rather than keeping the comparison separate.
The explanation only repeats the answer and says prayer is not mentioned. It needs a more natural explanation in Papa Dorin's voice.
The explanation repeats that Peter names the unstable without explaining what that means or adding any distinctive voice.
Peter names the unstable, but does not say they cannot also be wealthy.
Peter says the teachers follow Balaam's way and that Balaam loved the wages of wickedness. He does not specifically say their love of payment is the way they follow.
Peter says the teachers follow Balaam's way, not that they follow wages.
Daniel 6:16 supports the lion's den, but not the claim that Daniel was an exile. That detail needs a supporting reference.
The explanation only restates who is being enticed. It needs a little more explanation or distinctive voice.
Peter says they are escaping from others who live in error, not that they are already on their way out of error themselves.
Peter says the teachers promise freedom while being slaves themselves. He does not explicitly say what happens to the freedom they promise others.
Peter's condition includes being entangled and overcome again. The explanation makes entanglement alone enough for the stated outcome.
Peter includes being overcome as well as entangled. The explanation omits that condition and adds that Peter does not give them credit for escaping.
Comparing the sow returning to mud with an apron getting dirty makes light of the serious return to corruption the proverb illustrates.
The proverb says the sow was washed, but does not say the dog was clean. 'Neither of them stays clean' adds that detail.
